(2012) *3× First-team All-[[Atlantic Sun Conference|Atlantic Sun]] (2012–2014) *Atlantic Sun Freshman of the Year (2011) }} '''Torrey Craig''' (born December 19, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sydney Kings]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[USC Upstate Spartans men's basketball|USC Upstate Spartans]], where he was named an honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and [[Atlantic Sun Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Atlantic Sun Conference Player of the Year]] in 2012. After graduating from USC Upstate in 2014, Craig spent his first three professional seasons in Australia and New Zealand. He was named [[New Zealand NBL Most Valuable Player Award|New Zealand NBL MVP]] and won a [[List of New Zealand NBL champions|New Zealand NBL championship]] with the [[Wellington Saints]], and earned [[NBL Best Defensive Player Award|NBL Best Defensive Player]] honors with the [[Brisbane Bullets]]. In 2017, he began his NBA career with the [[Denver Nuggets]]. He has also played for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Chicago Bulls]], and [[Boston Celtics]]. In 2026, after joining the Sydney Kings in the middle of the season, Craig helped the team win the [[List of NBL champions|NBL championship]]. ==Early life== Craig was born in [[Columbia, South Carolina]],{{cite web | title = Torry Craig USC Upstate bio | work = [[USC Upstate Spartans]] | url = http://www.upstatespartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/bios/craig_torrey_8sg7 | access-date = November 16, 2013 | archive-date = February 25, 2019 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190225224002/https://www.upstatespartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/bios/craig_torrey_8sg7 | url-status = dead }} and raised in [[Great Falls, South Carolina]].{{cite web |last1=Mizell |first1=Gina |title=How Torrey Craig's childhood dream morphed into one of the NBA's most surprising success stories |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2018/05/04/torrey-craig-denver-nuggets-nba-story/ |website=The Denver Post |access-date=August 30, 2026 |date=May 4, 2018}} His mother, Teresa Mays, was imprisoned on drug charges when Craig was aged 5; she was released from jail when he was 21. His father was not part of his life. Craig was primarily raised by his grandmother, Daisy Mays, and his eldest sister, Sacha. He played basketball using a hoop that was mounted on a wooden streetlight. His grandmother died when Craig was in the eighth grade and Sacha became his legal guardian. Sacha arranged for him to move in with her where she was stationed at [[MacDill Air Force Base]] until two local coaches offered for Craig to live with them so he could stay in Great Falls and attend Great Falls High School. Craig was selected as the Class 1A Player of the Year in South Carolina during his senior season and led Great Falls to back-to-back state championship game appearances. ==College career== Craig played [[college basketball]] for the [[USC Upstate Spartans men's basketball|USC Upstate Spartans]]. As a freshman, Craig entered the starting lineup and quickly made an impact, averaging 14.4 [[Points per game|points]] and 7.2 [[rebounds per game]] en route to winning [[Atlantic Sun Conference]] Freshman of the Year honors.{{cite web | title = ETSU's Smith Headlines All-Conference Teams | work = [[Atlantic Sun Conference]] | date = March 1, 2011 | url = http://www.atlanticsun.org/mbasketball/news/2010-11/5138/etsus-smith-headlines-all-conference-teams/ | access-date = November 16, 2013 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140105045309/http://www.atlanticsun.org/mbasketball/news/2010-11/5138/etsus-smith-headlines-all-conference-teams/ | archive-date = January 5, 2014 }} In his sophomore season, Craig led the A-Sun in scoring at 16.4 points per game and helped the Spartans win 21 games. Craig was named the conference Player of the Year{{cite web | last = McCormick | first = Bret | title = Great Falls helped make USC Upstate's Craig into unassuming star | work = [[The Herald (Rock Hill)|The Herald]] | date = November 12, 2013 | url = http://www.heraldonline.com/2013/11/12/5399601/great-falls-helped-make-usc-upstates.html | access-date = November 16, 2013 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20131117024916/http://www.heraldonline.com/2013/11/12/5399601/great-falls-helped-make-usc-upstates.html | archive-date = November 17, 2013 | url-status = dead }} and an honorable mention All-American by the [[Associated Press]].{{cite web | title = Torrey Craig Named Honorable Mention AP All-American | work = [[USC Upstate Spartans]] | date = March 26, 2012 | url = http://www.upstatespartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/2011-12/releases/20120326xk08hz | access-date = November 16, 2013 | archive-date = December 29, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151229112124/http://www.upstatespartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/2011-12/releases/20120326xk08hz | url-status = dead }} As a junior, Craig once again led the A-Sun in scoring at 17.2 points per game. He was named first team All-Atlantic Sun. Prior to the start of his senior season, Craig was named preseason Player of the Year in the Atlantic Sun.{{cite web | last = Shanesy| first = Todd | title = USC Upstate's Craig named player of the year in preseason poll | work = [[Spartanburg Herald-Journal]] | date = October 10, 2013 | url = http://www.goupstate.com/article/20131010/ARTICLES/131019975 | access-date = November 16, 2013}} On February 10, 2014, Craig reached the 2,000 career point milestone with a 22-point game against [[2013–14 East Tennessee State Buccaneers basketball team|East Tennessee State]].{{cite web | title = Second Half Surge Leads Upstate Past ETSU | work = [[USC Upstate Spartans]] | date = February 10, 2014 | url = http://uscupstate.prestosports.com/sports/m-baskbl/2013-14/releases/20140210grjwm0 | access-date = February 13, 2014}} ==Professional career== ===Cairns Taipans and Wellington Saints (2014–2016)=== On August 6, 2014, Craig signed with the [[Cairns Taipans]] in Australia for the [[2014–15 NBL season]].{{cite news | last = Wenzel | first = Murray | title = South Carolina forward Torrey Craig is Cairns Taipans' latest recruit | work = CairnsPost.com.au | date = August 6, 2014 | url = http://www.cairnspost.com.au/sport/local-sport/south-carolina-forward-torrey-craig-is-cairns-taipans-latest-recruit/story-fnjpuwsz-1227015066306 | access-date = August 7, 2015}} Head coach [[Aaron Fearne]] encouraged Craig to focus on his defensive abilities which initially left him dissatisfied until he realised that he had the capacity to guard any assignment. Following the 2016–17 NBL season, Craig joined the [[Gold Coast Rollers (QBL)|Gold Coast Rollers]] of the [[Queensland Basketball League]].{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=Terry |url=http://www.goldcoastbulletin.com.au/sport/local-sport/gold-coast-rollers-sign-brisbane-bullets-star-torrey-craig-for-their-qbl-campaign/news-story/e4a4d4320bb9641e03dbc60711141b41 |title=Gold Coast Rollers sign Brisbane Bullets star Torrey Craig for their QBL campaign |work=GoldCoastBulletin.com.au |date=January 18, 2017 |access-date=January 18, 2017}}{{cite web |last=Royce |first=James |url=https://www.hit.com.au/news/gold-coast/nbl-star-signs-on-with-gold-coast-rollers/ |title=NBL star signs on with Gold Coast Rollers |work=Hit.com.au |date=January 18, 2017 |access-date=January 18, 2017}} He scored 30 points or more five times, including two 40-point games.{{cite web |url=http://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=203329403&client=1-4144-52768-451998-25991422 |title=Player statistics for Torrey Craig |work=SportsTG.com |access-date=July 20, 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170720060741/http://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=203329403&client=1-4144-52768-451998-25991422 |archive-date=July 20, 2017}} He was named Player of the Week for Round 3.{{cite web |url=http://qbl.basketballqld.com.au/player-week-round-3-2/ |title=Player of the Week – Round 3 |work=qbl.basketballqld.com.au |date=May 17, 2017 |access-date=May 17, 2017}} In 10 games for the Rollers, he averaged 28.2 points, 9.9 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.0 blocks per game. ===Denver Nuggets and Sioux Falls Skyforce (2017–2020)=== During his Bullets tenure, Craig was recommended to [[Tim Connelly]], president of basketball operations for the [[Denver Nuggets]], by his brother, Joe, the former coach of the [[Sydney Kings]]. Connelly gave Craig the chance to earn a contract, and Craig returned to the United States to join the Nuggets for [[2017 NBA Summer League|NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=Terry |url=http://www.goldcoastbulletin.com.au/sport/local-sport/gold-coast-rollers-resigned-to-losing-star-american-import-torrey-craig-to-the-nba/news-story/35eb834b5c4a583bde72fbc8195a5b6f |title=Gold Coast Rollers resigned to losing star American import Torrey Craig to the NBA |work=GoldCoastBulletin.com.au |date=June 28, 2017 |access-date=June 28, 2017}} On July 19, 2017, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Nuggets.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/sign-craig |title=Nuggets Sign Rookie Torrey Craig to Two-Way Contract |work=NBA.com |date=July 19, 2017 |access-date=July 19, 2017}}{{cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/denver-nuggets-strike-gold-torrey-craig/ |title=DENVER NUGGETS STRIKE GOLD WITH TORREY CRAIG |work=NBL.com.au |date=July 20, 2017 |last=Crouse |first=Chris |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2017/07/nuggets-to-sign-torrey-craig-to-two-way-deal.html |title=Nuggets Sign Torrey Craig To Two-Way Contract |work=HoopsRumors.com |date=July 19, 2017 |access-date=July 19, 2017}} Craig made his NBA debut on November 28, 2017, in the Nuggets' 106–77 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]],{{cite web|last=Dempsey|first=Christopher|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/story/craig-opportunity-g-league-nuggets-112917|title=Torrey Craig Making Most of Opportunity in G-League and With web|url=http://www.upstatespartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/2017-18/releases/20170717ob616u|title=Torrey Craig Earns Contract with Denver Nuggets|work=upstatespartans.com|date=July 17, agent]]. They withdrew the qualifying offer four days later, thus making him an unrestricted free agent.{{cite web|last=Adams|first=Luke|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2020/11/nuggets-withdraw-qo-for-torrey-craig-making-him-ufa.html|title=Nuggets Withdraw QO For Torrey Craig, Making Him UFA|work=hoopsrumors.com|date=November 21, 2020|access-date=November 22, 2020}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2020–2021)=== On November 26, 2020, Craig signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Bucks Sign Torrey Craig, Bryn Forbes and Bobby Portis |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-sign-torrey-craig-bryn-forbes-and-bobby-portis|date=November 26, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 26, 2020}} ===Phoenix Suns (2021)=== On March 18, 2021, Craig was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for cash considerations.{{cite web|title=SUNS ACQUIRE TORREY CRAIG FROM MILWAUKEE|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/suns-acquire-torrey-craig-milwaukee|date=March 18, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 18, 2021}} On April 25, 2021, he had 20 points and 14 rebounds off the bench against the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Torrey Craig 2020-21 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/craigto01/gamelog/2021|website=basketball-reference.com|access-date=July 4, 2021}} In the [[2021 NBA Finals]] against his former team the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], he averaged 2.8 points and 1.3 rebounds across the six games.
